# smpte-timecode

> SMPTE timecode arithmetic with exact drop-frame handling, and a MIDI Time Code decoder and
> encoder. `no_std`, no allocation, no dependencies, MSRV 1.85. Every public item is re-exported
> at the crate root: `use smpte_timecode::{...}`.

## Frame rates

- `FrameRate` is one of 19 rates: `FPS_23_976`, `FPS_24`, `FPS_25`, `FPS_29_97`, `FPS_29_97_DF`,
  `FPS_30`, `FPS_30_DF`, `FPS_47_952`, `FPS_48`, `FPS_50`, `FPS_59_94`, `FPS_59_94_DF`, `FPS_60`,
  `FPS_60_DF`, `FPS_100`, `FPS_119_88`, `FPS_119_88_DF`, `FPS_120`, `FPS_120_DF`. `FrameRate::ALL`
  lists them.
- `FrameRate::new(nominal: u8, ntsc: bool, drop_frame: bool)` looks one up; any other combination
  is `TimecodeError::UnsupportedFrameRate`.
- `nominal()` is the label count per second (24, 25, 30, 48, 50, 60, 100 or 120). `is_ntsc()`
  means frames run at 1000/1001 of nominal. `frames_per_second()` returns the exact `Ratio`.
  `frames_per_day()` counts the frames from midnight to midnight.
- Drop-frame rates (nominal 30, 60, 120) skip nominal/15 labels (2, 4, 8) at the start of each
  minute not divisible by ten. 29.97 DF and 59.94 DF are SMPTE ST 12-1. 30, 60, 119.88 and 120 DF
  follow the same rule as Pro Tools labels them.

## Timecode

- `Timecode` is a frame count from `00:00:00:00` within one day plus its `FrameRate`. It is `Copy`
  and `Eq`. Equality compares both the frame and the rate.
- Construction: `from_frames(u32, rate)` (`FrameOutOfRange` at or past `frames_per_day`),
  `from_fields(Fields, rate)`, `parse(&str, rate)`, `from_seconds(Ratio, rate, Rounding)`,
  `from_samples(u64, sample_rate: Ratio, rate, Rounding)`.
- `parse` accepts exactly `HH:MM:SS:FF` or, for drop-frame rates only, `HH:MM:SS;FF`. Hours,
  minutes and seconds have two digits; frames two or three. No surrounding whitespace. Drop-frame
  rates also accept `:`. Errors: `InvalidSyntax`, `DropFrameSeparator` (`;` at a non-drop rate),
  `FieldOutOfRange` (hours > 23, minutes or seconds > 59, frames >= nominal), `DroppedLabel`
  (for example `00:01:00;00` at 29.97 DF).
- `Display` writes `HH:MM:SS:FF`, with `;` before the frames at drop-frame rates, and at least two
  frame digits.
- `frames()`, `rate()`, `fields() -> Fields { hours, minutes, seconds, frames }` (all `u8`).
- `wrapping_add_frames(i64)` moves forward or backward and wraps at midnight for any `i64`.
- `to_seconds() -> Ratio` is exact. `to_samples(sample_rate: Ratio, Rounding) -> Result<u64>`
  rounds once at the end; `Overflow` if the sample does not fit `u64`.
- Converting from seconds or samples rounds to a frame with the given `Rounding`; errors are
  `ZeroSampleRate`, `Overflow` (128-bit intermediate) and `FrameOutOfRange` (past the day).
- With at least one sample per frame, `to_samples` with `Down` then `from_samples` with `Up`
  returns the original position, as do `Up`/`Down` and `Nearest`/`Nearest`.

## Ratio, Rounding, Pull

- `Ratio` is an exact non-negative rational in lowest terms with `u64` parts: `new(numer, denom)`
  (`ZeroDenominator` for 0), `from_integer`, `numer()`, `denom()`, `checked_mul -> Option`,
  `to_f64()` for display only, and total ordering by value.
- `Rounding::{Down, Up, Nearest}`. `Nearest` rounds exact halves up.
- `Pull` is an exact factor: `NONE`, `UP_0_1_PERCENT` (1001/1000), `DOWN_0_1_PERCENT`
  (1000/1001), `UP_4_PERCENT` (25/24), `DOWN_4_PERCENT` (24/25). `then(next) -> Option<Pull>`
  composes, `apply(Ratio) -> Option<Ratio>` multiplies a frame or sample rate, `factor()` exposes
  the ratio. `None` means the result does not fit `u64` parts.

## MIDI Time Code decoder

- `MtcDecoder::new()` (also `Default`), `with_quarter_frame_timeout(Duration)` (default 500 ms),
  `with_stale_after(Duration)` (default 1 s).
- `feed(&mut self, message: &[u8], at: Duration) -> Result<Option<MtcEvent>, MtcError>` takes one
  complete MIDI message and the time it arrived as a duration since any fixed instant. Use one
  clock per decoder. The decoder never reads a clock, allocates or blocks.
- Quarter frame `F1 0nnndddd`: a piece continues the cycle when it is one step after (forward) or
  before (reverse) the previous piece, modulo 8, within the timeout and in the same direction.
  Otherwise the cycle restarts at this piece. A position is produced when piece 7 (forward) or 0
  (reverse) completes eight collected pieces. Forward positions add two frames (RFC 6295 B.4) and
  wrap at midnight; reverse positions are as encoded. Reserved bits are masked.
- Full frame `F0 7F <device> 01 01 0rrhhhhh 00mmmmmm 00ssssss 000fffff F7`: any device ID; clears
  the quarter-frame cycle; produces a `Motion::Located` position without offset.
- Any other message, including user bits `F0 7F <device> 01 02 ...`, returns `Ok(None)` and leaves
  the state unchanged.
- Errors: `MtcError::MalformedMessage` (quarter frame not exactly two bytes or data byte >= 0x80;
  full frame not exactly ten bytes ending in F7, or a data byte >= 0x80) and
  `MtcError::InvalidTimecode(TimecodeError)` for a complete position that does not exist. The
  malformed message discards the partial cycle; an invalid complete position consumes the cycle.
  Neither error replaces or refreshes the last valid position.
- `MtcEvent { timecode: Timecode, motion: Motion, at: Duration }`.
  `Motion::{Forward, Reverse, Located}`.
- Rate codes: 0 → `FPS_24`, 1 → `FPS_25`, 2 → `FPS_29_97_DF`, 3 → `FPS_30`.
  `set_rate_hint(Option<FrameRate>)`: while the hint has the same `nominal()` as the code's rate,
  positions use the hint (recovers 23.976, 29.97 and 30 DF); otherwise the code's rate wins.
- `lock_state(now: Duration) -> LockState`: `Unlocked` before any position or after `reset()`;
  `Stale` when `now - at` of the last position exceeds the stale limit; otherwise
  `Locked(Motion)` of the last position.
- `reset()` clears the cycle and the last position, keeping limits and the rate hint.

## MIDI Time Code encoder

- `MtcEncoder::new(start: Timecode, Direction::{Forward, Reverse})`; rates with nominal 48 or more
  are `MtcError::NoRateCode`. Rate codes: nominal 24 → 0, 25 → 1, 30 drop-frame → 2, 30 → 3.
- `MtcEncoder` is an endless `Iterator<Item = [u8; 2]>` of quarter frames. Forward sends pieces
  0..=7 then advances two frames; reverse sends 7..=0 then moves back two frames; both wrap at
  midnight. `timecode()` is the position the current cycle carries.
- `quarter_frame_interval() -> Ratio` is the exact seconds between messages (a quarter frame).
  The caller times and sends the messages.
- `MtcEncoder::full_frame(Timecode) -> Result<[u8; 10], MtcError>` addresses device 0x7F.

## Not included

Subframes, LTC/VITC, MIDI port I/O, raw byte-stream SysEx assembly, user bits, MIDI Machine Control,
MIDI Cueing, speed estimation and freewheeling.
